children: Japanese government bond (JGB) yields fell on Thursday, with the 30-year yield retreating from a record high touched earlier this week, as investors remained cautious about the Bank of Japan's policy-tightening path ahead of a 30-year debt auction.
The benchmark 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 2.5 basis points (bps) to 3.080%, while the 30-year yield (JP30YTN=JBTC) declined 4 bps to 4.170%. Yields move inversely to bond prices.

The finance ministry is set to auction about 600 billion yen ($3.80 billion) of 30-year notes later in the day. The 30-year yield hit a record high of 4.25% on Monday over worries about Japan's worsening public finances and contagion from a French debt selloff

"Fiscal concerns remain a drag, but with yields high in absolute terms and near fair value based on longer-term moves and supply-demand conditions, we expect the auction to be uneventful," Barclays analysts said in a note.
The two-year yield (JP2YTN=JBTC), the one most sensitive to BOJ policy rates, decreased 1.5 bps to 1.93%. The five-year yield (JP5YTN=JBTC) fell 2 bps to 2.390%.
The 20-year JGB yield (JP20YTN=JBTC) slid 3.5 bps to 3.945%.
JGBs also tracked a retreat in global yields. US Treasury yields eased from multi-decade highs, as a strong 10-year note auction and a drop in oil prices tempered inflation concerns.

Market participants remained cautious over the BOJ tightening path, with expectations for another rate hike shifting towards December. While the BOJ may pause in October, it is likely to drop hawkish hints ⁠that would ​reinforce dominant market expectations of a December hike, sources have told Reuters.
The central bank will hold a regional branch managers' meeting and release a quarterly regional economic assessment report later in the day.
